subject: Burst beta: pool capacity commitment + pause conditions
body:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Jamal Pierce <jamal.pierce@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jun 6, 2025 at 9:14 AM PT
Subject: Burst beta: pool capacity commitment + pause conditions

Team,

Before we approve the June/July burst beta, I need an explicit capacity commitment per region/GPU type and the conditions under which we pause the beta (even if a pilot customer is “in flight”).

Two constraints:
1) We cannot risk hosted fleet commitments (esp. US-EAST peak hours).
2) We cannot create a situation where Dedicated baseline gets blamed for what is actually burst pool saturation.

Please reply with:
- Proposed burst pool headroom per region (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1) and GPU type (H100 vs A100/L40S, depending on what we’re using).
- What we consider the “hard stop” SRE signals (ex: sustained saturation, p99 drift on hosted, etc.).
- Who has the authority to hit the kill switch and what’s the expected SLA to do so.

Thanks,
Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Exec Sponsor (Infra/SRE)
Redwood Inference



From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Jamal Pierce <jamal.pierce@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jun 6, 2025 at 10:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Burst beta: pool capacity commitment + pause conditions

Neha / Priya,

Initial proposal (beta scope: 2–3 pilot tenants, US-only to start; EU optional if we get a pilot there).

Burst pools (separate labels + excluded from baseline Dedicated reservations):
- us-east-1: 16x H100 80GB equivalent
- us-west-2: 8x H100 80GB equivalent
- eu-west-1: 8x H100 80GB equivalent (optional; if enabled, only 1 tenant at first)

Rationale:
- us-east-1 is where we see the worst combined “hosted + dedicated” aggregate peak. We need enough to make burst meaningful, but not enough to eat into the buffer we use for hosted incidents.
- us-west-2 is primarily spillover + a couple of Dedicated tenants.
- eu-west-1 supply is tight. We can stand up a small pool but it should be the first to pause if things get weird.

Operational constraints / realities:
- Warmup: effectively ~30–60 minutes to bring new nodes to ready state; so “we’ll just add more” is not a mitigation in the moment.
- We can cap burst at the policy layer (TPS/concurrency) but routing has to honor the “deny” path cleanly.

Pause conditions (fleet side):
- If any region’s burst pool is >90% saturated (GPU utilization + queue depth) for >10 minutes AND reject rate >5% for the pilot tenant(s), we should pause onboarding new tenants into that region.
- If hosted oncall declares “capacity incident” for a region, burst should be disabled there immediately.

Kill switch:
- Fleet can disable via the existing pool label flip + routing weights, but we’d rather use the new per-tenant/per-region flag in the control plane for fast response.

Jamal is sanity-checking whether 16/8/8 is too high given current headroom. If it is, my fallback is 12/6/0 (EU off) for the first 2 weeks.

-Vanessa

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Fleet Lead, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference



From: Jamal Pierce <jamal.pierce@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jun 6, 2025 at 11:07 AM PT
Subject: Re: Burst beta: pool capacity commitment + pause conditions

Adding some numbers from capacity planning.

At current commit levels (Q3 forecast) we have ~18–22 H100 “effective” headroom in us-east-1 during non-peak, but only ~10–14 during peak (depending on hosted batch jobs).

If we allocate 16 H100 to burst in us-east-1, we’re basically saying:
- Peak: we’ll be running close to the line; any hosted incident response that needs that buffer becomes “disable burst now” rather than “we have slack.”

My recommendation for the first 30 days:
- us-east-1: 12x H100
- us-west-2: 6x H100
- eu-west-1: 0x H100 (hold until we have a named EU pilot + explicit supply confirmation)

This still lets us offer meaningful burst (especially if pilots are on strict policy caps), but it preserves incident headroom for hosted.

Re pause conditions: I like Vanessa’s >90% saturation + rejects, but I’d add a “hosted p99 drift” guardrail (SRE should define exact numbers).

-Jamal

—
Jamal Pierce
Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Jamal Pierce <jamal.pierce@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jun 6, 2025 at 12:21 PM PT
Subject: Re: Burst beta: pool capacity commitment + pause conditions

From SRE perspective, I want two separate concepts:
A) “Pause beta onboarding” (no new tenants/regions)
B) “Disable burst” (stop admitting burst traffic for an existing tenant)

Hard stop signals (disable burst in region immediately):
1) Hosted fleet SLO risk:
   - Hosted p99 latency +20% sustained for 10 minutes correlated with burst pool draw OR
   - Hosted error rate (5xx) +0.5% absolute for 5 minutes where capacity pressure is a suspected factor.
2) Neighbor risk / noisy neighbor indicator:
   - Any Dedicated baseline tenant in same region shows p99 drift +25% for 10 minutes AND we can correlate to burst saturation.
3) Burst pool instability:
   - Burst pool saturation >95% for 10 minutes OR queue depth crossing the “drop threshold” (we’ll define in dashboard) AND admission rejects >10%.

Pause onboarding signals:
- Burst rejects >5% for >30 minutes during normal operation (i.e., not game day), or
- Two “disable burst” events in the same week.

Authority:
- Oncall SRE (primary) can disable per-tenant/per-region burst in <10 minutes.
- Fleet oncall can also disable at the pool/routing level if control plane is unhealthy.
- We should have an explicit “permissioned CLI” path (INT-881) so we’re not blocked on access during an incident.

Operational ask:
If we go with Jamal’s 12/6/0 numbers, we can set an expectation in the beta terms that EU is not supported initially and that US regions can be paused without notice for reliability.

-Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Jamal Pierce <jamal.pierce@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jun 6, 2025 at 1:18 PM PT
Subject: Re: Burst beta: pool capacity commitment + pause conditions

+1 to splitting “pause onboarding” vs “disable.”

From product/customer side, we can message:
- Burst is best-effort capacity with strict admission control.
- We may temporarily disable burst for reliability/neighbor protection (no SLA on burst itself during beta).
- Regions supported in beta: US only.

Two questions so I can finalize the pilot terms:
1) For US, are we comfortable committing that “burst will be available most of the time” (e.g., target >95% admission success when under customer’s configured limits), or are we explicitly not making any admission target in beta?
2) When we disable burst due to hosted incident, do we expect to re-enable automatically (after cooldown) or require human sign-off? I’d prefer human sign-off for the first month.

If we align on 12/6/0 capacity and Sean’s stop conditions, I can incorporate into the exec approval note + customer beta addendum.

Thanks,
Lauren

—
Lauren Bishop
Product DRI (Dedicated)
Redwood Inference



From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Jamal Pierce <jamal.pierce@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jun 6, 2025 at 2:46 PM PT
Subject: Re: Burst beta: pool capacity commitment + pause conditions

Aligning on a conservative start.

Decision (for beta approval):
- Capacity commitment (initial 30 days):
  - us-east-1: 12x H100 equivalent
  - us-west-2: 6x H100 equivalent
  - eu-west-1: 0 (no EU beta until we have a named pilot + supply confirmation)

- Stop conditions: use Sean’s set as the “disable burst immediately” triggers. If any trigger hits, burst is disabled in-region for all beta tenants until SRE lead (or delegate) explicitly re-enables.

- Target admission success rate:
  - For beta, no external commitment/guarantee. Internally, we should track admission success rate under configured limits and aim for >=95% in steady state, but we should not promise this to customers yet.

- Authority:
  - Oncall SRE can disable (per tenant/per region); fleet oncall can disable pools/routing as fallback. INT-881 to make sure access is not fragile.

Neha: if you’re good with this framing, we can treat this as the “capacity & safety gates” section of the exec sign-off.

-Priya

—
Priya Natarajan
Exec Sponsor (Platform)
Redwood Inference



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Jamal Pierce <jamal.pierce@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jun 6, 2025 at 4:38 PM PT
Subject: Re: Burst beta: pool capacity commitment + pause conditions

Approved with the numbers + gates as written.

A few explicit notes for the record:
- EU is out of scope for beta until we say otherwise.
- If hosted oncall declares a capacity incident, burst gets disabled first; no debate.
- Re-enable requires human sign-off for the first month (Sean or delegate). After we have 2 weeks of clean metrics, we can revisit auto re-enable.

Lauren: please bake the above into the beta terms and customer expectations.
Vanessa/Jamal: please ensure the 12/6 capacity is “real” (reserved at the fleet level) and not a planning fiction.
Sean: make sure the runbook includes the exact disable commands + the “who can do it” path (INT-881).

Thanks everyone.

-Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Exec Sponsor (Infra/SRE)
Redwood Inference
